# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
# Copyright (C) 2026 Busbar Inc and contributors
#
# busbar deployment configuration (config.yaml).
#
# Two-file model:
#   • providers.yaml  — the vetted provider catalog (protocol, base_url, error_map). Shipped.
#   • config.yaml     — THIS file: your deployment. References providers by NAME and supplies their
#                       keys as SECRET REFERENCES (never the keys themselves).
#
# Flow: clients call busbar; busbar routes each request to a `model` or a `pool` of models, tracks
# per-member health with a circuit breaker, and translates between protocols when a client speaks a
# different wire format than the chosen backend. Secrets are never written here - every secret value
# is a SECRET REFERENCE resolved through a secret module: `{ env: VAR }` (environment variable),
# `{ file: /path }` (file contents), or `{ module: <secret-plugin>, settings: {…} }`.
#
# This example builds up from the simplest case to progressively richer pools — read top to bottom.

# ── Listen address ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
listen: "0.0.0.0:8080"

# ── Admin plane (always its own listener) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The admin API (/api/v1/admin/…) ALWAYS runs on its OWN listener — it is never served on the data
# `listen` above. The management plane is privileged, so it stays isolated with its own TLS/mTLS,
# bind, and firewall posture, independent of public LLM traffic. `admin_listen` defaults to loopback
# (127.0.0.1:8081), so a zero-config deployment boots with admin reachable only on-host.
#
# SECURITY: a network-exposed admin_listen (any non-loopback bind) REFUSES TO BOOT unless it requires
# client-certificate mTLS via admin_tls.client_ca. A loopback bind (127.0.0.1 / ::1 / localhost)
# is exempt. To run a token-only admin plane on an exposed address on purpose — e.g. behind a mesh
# that terminates mTLS — set `admin_require_mtls: false` to waive the guard deliberately.
#
# admin_listen: "127.0.0.1:8081"    # default; set an exposed address (+ admin_tls) to manage off-host
# admin_tls:
#   cert:      { file: /etc/busbar/admin-cert.pem }
#   key:       { file: /etc/busbar/admin-key.pem }
#   client_ca: { file: /etc/busbar/admin-client-ca.pem }   # present ⇒ mTLS required on the admin plane
# admin_require_mtls: true                               # false ⇒ waive the exposed-admin mTLS guard

# ── busbar AS an OAuth 2.1 authorization server (oauth_as:) ──────────────────────────────────────
# ABSENT BY DEFAULT, and absent means nothing is built: no server, no store, no signing key, no
# background sweep and no route. Uncomment it only if agents must log in to busbar WITHOUT an
# identity provider - which is the case Codex, ChatGPT and Claude.ai are in, because enterprise IdPs
# do not enable RFC 7591 dynamic client registration.
#
# With an IdP, leave this out: busbar is the OAuth RESOURCE server, tokens come from Okta/Entra/
# Auth0, and `mcp.authorization_servers` names them. The two modes are independent and both ship.
#
# oauth_as:
#   # RFC 8414 `issuer`: this authorization server's identity, and the base every endpoint is
#   # derived from - `{issuer}/authorize`, `{issuer}/token`, `{issuer}/jwks`, `{issuer}/consent`,
#   # and `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` with the issuer's PATH appended AFTER it
#   # (RFC 8414 s3.1 puts the well-known segment first; RFC 9728 puts it last - the two documents
#   # this deployment serves build their paths in opposite orders).
#   # No trailing slash, no query, no fragment: all three are boot refusals, because RFC 9207 has
#   # clients compare this value byte-for-byte.
#   issuer: "https://gw.example.com"
#
#   # The ES256 signing key: base64 of a PKCS#8 v1 DER P-256 private key. Produce one with
#   #   openssl genpkey -algorithm EC -pkeyopt ec_paramgen_curve:P-256 -outform DER | base64
#   # OMITTED is legal and generates an EPHEMERAL key at boot, with a warning: every token the
#   # deployment issued stops verifying when the process restarts. Fine for a trial, wrong for
#   # anything else. There is deliberately no default key - a default would be a published private
#   # key that signs valid tokens for every deployment that never set this field.
#   signing_key: { env: BUSBAR_AS_SIGNING_KEY }
#
#   # WHAT A SELF-REGISTERED CLIENT GETS, AND NOTHING MORE. Empty by default, so a client that
#   # registers itself and asks for a scope is REFUSED (`invalid_client_metadata`) rather than
#   # quietly narrowed. This is a ceiling, and nothing at runtime moves it.
#   default_grant: []
#
#   # There is NO registration toggle. With `oauth_as:` configured, all three ways a client
#   # obtains a client_id are ON: pre-registration, Client ID Metadata Documents, and RFC 7591
#   # dynamic client registration at {issuer}/register. What keeps that safe is the ceiling
#   # above: registration confers nothing beyond `default_grant`, which is empty until you
#   # widen it.
#
#   # Access token lifetime in seconds; default 600, at most 86400. Short on purpose - clients refresh.
#   access_token_ttl_secs: 600
#
#   # Refresh chain lifetime in seconds, absolute (rotation keeps the first expiry); default
#   # 2592000 (30 days), at most 31536000 (a year).
#   refresh_token_ttl_secs: 2592000
#
#   # The FAPI 2.0 Security Profile posture (plain OAuth, private_key_jwt, DPoP); default false.
#   # true makes RFC 9126 pushed authorization requests MANDATORY at {issuer}/par (with
#   # redirect_uri required), requires an RFC 9449 DPoP proof on every token request, reuses
#   # refresh tokens rather than rotating them, accepts a client assertion only with aud = the
#   # issuer as a string, and verifies ES256/PS256 only. Every client must then speak all of it.
#   fapi2: false
#
#   # Confidential private_key_jwt (RFC 7523) clients you provision yourself; none by default.
#   # Registration over the wire cannot carry a key, so this is how a FAPI 2.0 client gets a
#   # client_id. PUBLIC keys only, EC P-256 (ES256) or RSA of 2048+ bits (PS256), one algorithm per
#   # client; a key carrying `d` is refused.
#   # Each client may ask for no more than default_grant.
#   clients:
#     - client_id: payments-app
#       redirect_uris: ["https://app.example.com/cb"]
#       jwks: { keys: [ { kty: EC, crv: P-256, kid: k1, x: "<base64url>", y: "<base64url>" } ] }

# ── Client authentication ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# identity-providers - DEFINE each identity provider ONCE (name -> {module, settings,
# max_admin_scope, token}); auth.chain / auth.admin_auth / role_bindings then REFERENCE it BY BARE
# NAME. The built-ins `keys` (signed-key verifier) and `admin-tokens` (operator credential) are
# referenced bare and need a definition only when they carry config.
identity-providers:
  admin-tokens: { module: admin-tokens, token: { env: BUSBAR_ADMIN_TOKEN } }
  # corp-ad:
  #   module: ad
  #   settings: { server: "ldaps://corp", base_dn: "dc=corp" }
  #   max_admin_scope: read-only # per-provider ADMIN ceiling; `read-only` | `full` ONLY.
  #                              # OMIT it for read-only, the most restrictive default.

# auth.chain - an ORDERED list of identity-provider NAMES identifying the caller. `keys` is the
# built-in signed-key verifier: clients present busbar-minted keys (POST /api/v1/admin/keys).
# An EMPTY chain is an open relay (no client auth; dev only). admin_auth gates /api/v1/admin/*
# (default [admin-tokens]); role_bindings map a provider's asserted ROLES to policy (allowed_pools /
# group / admin_scope), NESTED BY PROVIDER NAME. Whose key hits the provider is
# `pools.upstream_credentials` (see the pools section), not an auth concern.
auth:
  chain: [keys]
  admin_auth: [admin-tokens]                                 # guards the admin API (mint keys etc.)
  # role_bindings:
  #   corp-ad:
  #     growth-eng: { allowed_pools: [fast], group: growth }
  #     platform:   { group: acme, admin_scope: full }       # allowed_pools omitted = ALL pools
  #     auditors:   { verbs: [get_audit, get_ledger_totals] } # per-verb admin allow-list ("*" = full)
  signing_key: { file: /var/lib/busbar/signing.key }        # REQUIRED with `keys` above; fleet-shared
  #                                                          # key. Generate: `busbar --generate-signing-key`.

# ── Providers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Reference a provider NAME from providers.yaml and give a secret reference for its key. protocol /
# base_url / error_map are inherited from providers.yaml; override here only in unusual cases.
providers:
  anthropic:
    api_key: { env: ANTHROPIC_KEY }
    # Optional active health probing for this provider's lanes (default: no probing — health is
    # inferred from real traffic via the breaker + half-open probe).
    #   mode: none   — passive only (default).
    #        dead   — periodically re-probe ONLY tripped lanes so they recover faster.
    #        active — periodically probe EVERY lane (sends a tiny billable request per interval).
    # health:
    #   mode: dead
    #   interval_secs: 30   # default 30
    #   timeout_secs: 5     # default 5
  openai:
    api_key: { env: OPENAI_KEY }
  gemini:
    api_key: { env: GEMINI_KEY }
  z.ai:
    api_key: { env: ZAI_KEY }
  bedrock:
    # Bedrock auth is AWS SigV4: the secret holds `ACCESS_KEY_ID:SECRET_ACCESS_KEY[:SESSION_TOKEN]`.
    api_key: { env: AWS_BEDROCK_CREDS }

# ── Models ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Each model names its provider, a per-model concurrency cap (max_concurrent), and an optional
# lifetime request budget (max_requests; -1 = unlimited). A model is a "lane" with its own semaphore
# and health state. Clients can target a model directly (`POST /<model>/v1/messages`) or via a pool.
#
# default_max_tokens (optional): output-token default injected ONLY when a cross-protocol translation
# targets a backend that REQUIRES max_tokens (the Anthropic Messages API) and the source request
# omitted it — legal for OpenAI clients, which rely on the server default. Without it, such a request
# 400s with `max_tokens: Field required`. Unset falls back to a conservative 4096; a caller-supplied
# max_tokens is always preserved. No effect on same-protocol passthrough. Must be > 0 when set.
# (Bedrock Converse defaults maxTokens when omitted, so it needs no injection.)
models:
  claude-sonnet:
    provider: anthropic
    max_concurrent: 20
    max_requests: -1
    # default_max_tokens: 4096   # backfill when an OpenAI client omits max_tokens (else 4096)
    # reasoning: true   # declare that THIS model accepts thinking params: with it, a translated
    #                   # reasoning ask (OpenAI reasoning_effort / Gemini thinkingBudget) reaches
    #                   # this lane as Anthropic thinking{budget_tokens}; without it the ask is
    #                   # dropped (warned) and never sent, so a non-thinking model never 400s.
  claude-haiku:
    provider: anthropic
    max_concurrent: 40
    max_requests: -1
  gpt-4o:
    provider: openai
    max_concurrent: 20
    max_requests: -1
  gpt-4o-mini:
    provider: openai
    max_concurrent: 50
    max_requests: -1
  gemini-1.5-pro:
    provider: gemini
    max_concurrent: 15
    max_requests: -1
  glm-4.6:
    provider: z.ai
    max_concurrent: 10
    max_requests: -1
  claude-sonnet-bedrock:
    provider: bedrock
    max_concurrent: 20
    max_requests: -1

# ── Pools ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# A pool is a named set of weighted member models. Its members' concurrency caps stack into one
# aggregate, and the breaker fails a request over to a healthy member when one is tripped. Target a
# pool with `POST /<pool>/v1/messages` (or the `model` field for `/v1/chat/completions`).
pools:

  # RESERVED section keys (1.5.3, and this set is CLOSED — a pool may not be named either of them):
  #   hooks:                — attach these hooks to ALL pools (a LIST, so it is ADDITIVE with a
  #                            pool's own `hooks:`; a name in both fires ONCE, at its first position)
  #   upstream_credentials: — the ALL-POOLS default for whose key hits the provider: `own` (busbar's
  #                            configured key) or `passthrough` (forward the caller's). A SCALAR, so
  #                            a pool's own value REPLACES it.
  upstream_credentials: own

  # 1) Simplest pool: a single model. Useful to give a model a stable public name / alias.
  haiku:
    members:
      - model: claude-haiku

  # 2) Basic round-robin: equal-weight members. Smooth weighted round-robin spreads load evenly;
  #    if one member trips, traffic shifts to the others automatically.
  fast:
    members:
      - model: claude-haiku
      - model: gpt-4o-mini

  # 3) Weighted split: send ~80% to the first member, ~20% to the second (e.g. canarying a model).
  balanced:
    members:
      - model: claude-sonnet
        weight: 8
      - model: gpt-4o
        weight: 2

  # 4) Context-length aware: declare each member's max context window. A request that is too large
  #    for one member fails over to a larger-context member instead of erroring — without penalizing
  #    the smaller lane (it was healthy; the request simply didn't fit).
  long-context:
    members:
      - model: claude-sonnet
        context_max: 200000
      - model: gemini-1.5-pro
        context_max: 2000000

  # 5) Failover tuning: bound how long/often busbar retries across members for one request.
  #    timeout_secs — give up after this wall-clock budget. max_hops — at most this many failover hops.
  #    exclusions — member models to never fail a request over TO (e.g. an expensive last resort).
  resilient:
    members:
      - model: claude-sonnet
        weight: 3
      - model: gpt-4o
        weight: 2
      - model: glm-4.6
        weight: 1
    failover:
      timeout_secs: 30
      max_hops: 3
      exclusions:
        - glm-4.6        # kept in the pool for capacity, but never used as a failover destination

  # 5b) Per-attempt hang cap (attempt_timeout_ms): some providers fail by HANGING — the connection
  #     opens and headers never come back, silently eating the whole failover budget on one member.
  #     attempt_timeout_ms caps a single attempt's time to RESPONSE HEADERS; on expiry the attempt
  #     counts as a transient breaker failure and the request hops to the next member immediately.
  #     It never cuts a stream that has started answering (covers connect + headers only).
  #     Two layers: set it on a model (models.<name>.attempt_timeout_ms) as that model's default
  #     everywhere, and/or on a pool member to override per pool — so the SAME model can get 10s in
  #     a batch pool and 50ms in a latency-critical one. 0 is a startup error; omit to disable.
  realtime:
    members:
      - model: gemini-1.5-pro
        attempt_timeout_ms: 250   # this pool is time-critical: hop if no headers in 250ms
      - model: claude-haiku      # fallback lane picks the request up in-flight

  # 6) Exhaustion policy + fallback pool: when every member is tripped/at-capacity, choose what to do.
  #    on_exhausted: reject | least_bad | { fallback_pool: <name> }
  #      least_bad      — serve the member whose cooldown expires soonest rather than 503.
  #      fallback_pool  - route to another pool entirely (loop-guarded; a structured reference).
  primary:
    members:
      - model: claude-sonnet
      - model: gpt-4o
    on_exhausted: { fallback_pool: overflow }   # when primary is fully exhausted, spill to `overflow`

  # The fallback pool referenced above. Its own exhaustion policy serves the soonest-healthy member.
  overflow:
    members:
      - model: claude-haiku
      - model: gpt-4o-mini
      - model: glm-4.6
    on_exhausted: least_bad

  # 7) Session affinity + cross-protocol: pin a conversation to one member while it's healthy (so
  #    cache/state stays warm), keyed by a request header. Members here span THREE protocols
  #    (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini) — a client speaking any one of them reaches all three, because
  #    busbar translates losslessly through its superset IR.
  smart:
    members:
      - model: claude-sonnet
        weight: 2
      - model: gpt-4o
        weight: 2
      - model: gemini-1.5-pro
        weight: 1
    affinity:
      mode: session              # stick to one member per session while it stays healthy
      header_name: x-session-id  # the request header carrying the session key (this is the default)

  # 8) Per-pool circuit breaker: tune when a member trips out and how long it cools down. Omit the
  #    block entirely for the ADR-0002 defaults (error_rate, 0.5 over a 30s/5-request floor).
  #      trip.mode        — error_rate (fraction of failures in a window) | consecutive (a streak).
  #      trip.window_secs - sliding window for error_rate.
  #      trip.threshold   — error fraction that trips (error_rate mode).
  #      trip.min_requests— floor: never trip on error_rate below this many outcomes in-window.
  #      trip.consecutive_n - consecutive failures that trip (consecutive mode).
  #      base/max_cooldown_secs — first cooldown after a trip, and the exponential-backoff ceiling.
  #    (A server Retry-After header is always honored as a cooldown floor, on top of these.)
  sensitive:
    members:
      - model: claude-sonnet
      - model: gpt-4o
    breaker:
      trip:
        mode: consecutive        # trip fast on a short streak rather than a windowed rate
        consecutive_n: 2         # two consecutive failures trip the member out
      base_cooldown_secs: 5      # quick first probe-back…
      max_cooldown_secs: 60      # …backing off exponentially up to a minute

# ── MCP: busbar as an MCP server (optional; ABSENT by default) ───────────────────────────────────
# Presence of this block is what makes this deployment an MCP server. Absent, busbar mounts no MCP
# ingress and no `.well-known` document at all — a gateway that is not an MCP server does not answer
# as one.
#
# WHAT AN AGENT DOES, end to end, with no prior configuration:
#   1. It POSTs to the endpoint with no credential and gets `401` with
#      `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer resource_metadata="…/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp"`.
#   2. It fetches that document (RFC 9728) and learns which authorization servers may mint tokens
#      for this resource, and what this resource calls itself.
#   3. It does ordinary OAuth against your IdP, asking for a token whose audience is `canonical_uri`.
#   4. It comes back, and busbar checks the token's audience is ITSELF before anything else happens.
#
# busbar is the RESOURCE SERVER here, never the authorization server: the tokens are minted by your
# existing IdP (Okta, Entra, Auth0) and nothing in busbar issues one.
#
# mcp:
#   # The RFC 8707 resource indicator. This is THE audience every inbound token must carry, compared
#   # for exact equality. Its path MUST be `/mcp`: the endpoint is served there and nowhere else,
#   # and a URI naming any other path refuses boot. The scheme, host and port are yours. It is
#   # configured rather than taken from the request's Host header on purpose: deriving it from the
#   # request would let a caller choose its own audience, which is the whole defence, undone.
#   canonical_uri: "https://gateway.example.com/mcp"
#
#   # Your IdP's issuer(s), advertised in the metadata document. At least one is REQUIRED: it is the
#   # entire content of the answer a client with no credential came here for.
#   authorization_servers:
#     - "https://login.example.com"
#
#   # Advisory metadata. Authorization is decided by the caller's grant, never by this list.
#   scopes_supported: ["mcp:tools:list", "mcp:tools:call"]
#
#   # Browser origins accepted on the ingress (the DNS-rebinding defence). EMPTY IS THE DEFAULT and
#   # it means no browser origin is accepted. Agents send no `Origin` at all and are unaffected;
#   # loopback origins are always accepted, because a browser only sends one for a document served
#   # from loopback, which the rebinding attacker's page never is.
#   allowed_origins: []

# ── Observability (optional) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# ALL telemetry egress is the single `export:` NAMED map (1.5.3): `<name>: { module, settings }`,
# presence = the switch. Zero-config default: collection is inert. The four built-in modules:
#   prometheus          — PULL: install the recorder + serve `/metrics` (buffer_seconds REQUIRED).
#   request-log-webhook — PUSH: fire-and-forget a JSON request-log POST per request (https-only);
#                          optional `auth_header: { name, value }`.
#   request-log-file    — PUSH: append each request-log line as JSONL.
#   otlp                — export OpenTelemetry traces (OTLP/HTTP) to a collector.
# The SAME module may back SEVERAL named instances — e.g. two webhooks to two URLs:
# export:
#   metrics:  { module: prometheus,          settings: { buffer_seconds: 60, key_gauge_limit: 2000 } }
#   req-log:  { module: request-log-webhook, settings: { url: "https://logs.example.com/busbar" } }
#   req-siem: { module: request-log-webhook, settings: { url: "https://siem.internal/ingest" } }
#   traces:   { module: otlp,                settings: { url: "http://localhost:4318/v1/traces" } }

# ── Response headers (optional; see docs/observability.md#response-headers) ────────────────────────
# Every busbar-INJECTED response header is an opt-in toggle under `advanced.response_headers`, default
# OFF (each is an in-band busbar fingerprint, off by design so none can undercut backend
# indistinguishability). Restart-to-apply.
#   server_timing  — emit `Server-Timing: busbar;dur=<ms>` (busbar's own added latency).
#   route_policy   — emit `x-busbar-route-policy` / `x-busbar-route-target` when a non-default
#                    routing policy chose the lane.
# advanced:
#   response_headers:
#     server_timing: true
#     route_policy: true

# ── Groups: the ONE limit tree (optional) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Named enforcement buckets forming an acyclic tree (parent chains AND together). A
# minted key binds to at most one group; a key with no group is authed + unlimited. Generic limits:
# each is `{ <metric>: <amount>, per: <window> }` with metric one of requests|tokens|budget|
# concurrent and window one of minute|hour|day|month|total (`concurrent` is instantaneous: no per).
# `enabled: false` freezes a group (history kept).
# groups:
#   acme:
#     limits:
#       - { requests: 500, per: minute }
#       - { budget: 10000000, per: month }
#   growth:
#     parent: acme
#     limits:
#       - { budget: 2000000, per: month }
#       - { concurrent: 50 }

# ── Pricing: the ONE cost source (optional) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Per-model token pricing in MICRO-units per token (abstract cost units - busbar attaches no
# currency). ALL-OR-NOTHING at two levels: absent = billing off (tokens price 0); present = EVERY
# configured model needs an entry (--validate prints a paste-ready stub otherwise), AND every
# billable class the LLM plane declares must be configured on some entry — the four reserved
# *_utok tiers below count as configured just by the card's presence (an omitted tier is 0), but
# the OPEN classes are not reserved and each needs an explicit `units: { <class>: <rate> }` on at
# least one entry; `0` makes one free but still counts as configured. The LLM plane ledgers every
# count a provider reports beside its tokens under its own open class: `search_units` (a rerank's
# search units, an Anthropic turn's web searches), `classifications` (Cohere), `web_fetch_requests`
# (Anthropic), `unitemized_tokens` (the tokens a provider's stated total counts above its itemized
# buckets), `images` (per-image answers), `audio_ms` (a transcription's reported duration) and the
# nine Bedrock `guardrail_*` policy-unit classes. A card silent about a declared class fails boot
# naming it. Keys are the CONFIG model names above.
#
# UPGRADING FROM 1.5.5: a card that priced only the four reserved tiers (no `units:` at all) now
# fails boot. Add the `units:` below to any one entry (0 keeps each free, as 1.5.5 billed them).
# rate_card:
#   claude-sonnet: { input_utok: 3.0, output_utok: 15.0, cache_read_utok: 0.3, cache_write_utok: 3.75,
#                    units: { search_units: 0, classifications: 0, web_fetch_requests: 0,
#                             unitemized_tokens: 0, images: 0, audio_ms: 0,
#                             guardrail_automated_reasoning_policies: 0,
#                             guardrail_automated_reasoning_policy_units: 0,
#                             guardrail_content_policy_image_units: 0, guardrail_content_policy_units: 0,
#                             guardrail_contextual_grounding_policy_units: 0,
#                             guardrail_sensitive_information_policy_free_units: 0,
#                             guardrail_sensitive_information_policy_units: 0,
#                             guardrail_topic_policy_units: 0, guardrail_word_policy_units: 0 } }
#   gpt-4o:        { input_utok: 2.5, output_utok: 10.0 }
# per_request_fee: 0                       # flat per-request budget charge (default 0)
#
# Non-LLM planes take the SAME reserved `rate_card` key under their OWN section instead — e.g.
# `tools.rate_card` (MCP, keyed by tool name, prices `tool_calls`/`bytes`) or `agents.rate_card`
# (A2A, keyed `agent:<id>`, prices `bytes` = request + response body bytes per hop) — each
# independent of this flat card and of each other; see docs/mcp.md and docs/a2a.md. A plane
# section with no card of its own bills that plane's traffic at 0 (no refusal).

# ── Store (required) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Where keys/usage/audit live: `{ module, settings }`. `memory` is the compiled-in RAM store (keys/
# usage reset on restart). A config with no `store:` block is refused; `busbar --migrate-config`
# inserts `store: { module: memory }`. A non-memory module requires plugins.enabled below; settings
# are the module's own config, passed through verbatim.
store:
  module: memory
# store:
#   module: sqlite                          # busbar-store-sqlite (single-node durable)
#   settings: { db_path: /var/lib/busbar/governance.db }
# store:
#   module: postgres                        # cluster-shared keys/usage/audit

# ── Advanced (optional) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Internal tuning; the defaults are right for almost everyone.
# advanced:
#   rate_sweep_interval: 256                # rate-map idle-entry sweep amortization
#   usage_flush_interval_ms: 100            # write-behind flush cadence for usage counters

# ── Plugins (optional; OFF by default) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The dynamic plugin subsystem: signed plugin tarballs ({cdylib + manifest.json} as one .tar.gz)
# that busbar verifies and loads at boot. With `enabled: false` (or this block absent) NO plugin
# ever loads - a tarball dropped in the directory is inert. busbar's own release key is EMBEDDED in
# the binary, so busbar-signed plugins verify with zero configuration; the trust block is for
# third-party publishers and explicit opt-ins. Validate ahead of boot with `busbar --validate`;
# inspect with `busbar --list-plugins`. See docs/plugins.md.
# plugins:
#   enabled: true                            # MASTER SWITCH (default false)
#   dir: plugins                             # where the signed .tar.gz tarballs live
#   trust:
#     publishers:                            # third-party ed25519 signing keys (allowlist)

#     allow_third_party: false               # explicit opt-in for non-allowlisted publishers
#   min_versions:                            # anti-downgrade floors by manifest name (third-party;
#     acme-store-dynamo: "2.0.0"             # first-party is auto-floored at the binary version)

# Demo: Claude Code (Anthropic protocol) → Busbar → Amazon Nova on Bedrock.
# The agent speaks Anthropic; Busbar translates to Bedrock Converse and back.
listen: "127.0.0.1:8080"
admin_listen: "127.0.0.1:8081"

# Signed-key auth: mint a key via the admin API (POST /api/v1/admin/keys) and give it to the
# agent as its bearer token. An empty chain would be an open relay (dev only).
# 1.5.3: an identity provider is DEFINED once here and REFERENCED by bare name in the chains.
identity-providers:
  admin-tokens: { module: admin-tokens, token: { env: BUSBAR_ADMIN_TOKEN } }

auth:
  chain: [keys]                # bare provider NAMES; `keys` is the built-in signed-key verifier
  # REQUIRED whenever the chain names `keys` (1.5.1+ no longer auto-generates one, and validate/boot
  # fail closed without it). Mint the file with `busbar --generate-signing-key > <path>`; a fleet
  # shares ONE key, and rotating it revokes every outstanding virtual key.
  signing_key: { env: BUSBAR_SIGNING_KEY }
  admin_auth: [admin-tokens]

# Response headers busbar injects are opt-in and default OFF; see
# docs/observability.md#response-headers. This demo opts into the latency probe.
advanced:
  response_headers:
    server_timing: true

# A store is required in 1.6.0 (`busbar --migrate-config` inserts this); memory is ephemeral RAM.
store:
  module: memory

providers:
  bedrock:
    api_key: { env: AWS_BEDROCK_CREDS }

models:
  amazon-nova:
    provider: bedrock
    max_concurrent: 10
    max_requests: -1
    upstream_model: amazon.nova-pro-v1:0   # the real Bedrock modelId that answers

pools:
  upstream_credentials: own    # 1.5.3: reserved all-pools key (was auth.upstream_credentials)
  claude-code:
    members:
      - model: amazon-nova
        weight: 1
name: file:examples/claude-code-bedrock/config.yaml

input:
# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
# Copyright (C) 2026 Busbar Inc and contributors
#
# The 1.5.0 CLEAN CONFIG example: the full redesigned surface in one file, shaped so that
# `busbar --validate` passes against the shipped providers.yaml with no plugins installed and
# no secrets present:
#   - the store uses the compiled-in `memory` module (a durable store is a plugin tarball),
#   - the auth chain is the built-in `keys` verifier (an IdP module is a `kind: auth` plugin),
#   - hook instances are the bare built-ins (an out-of-process hook is an inline module ref),
#   - numeric literals carry no underscore separators (YAML ints are plain digits).
#
# Validate with:
#   BUSBAR_CONFIG=examples/clean-config-1.5.0.yaml busbar --validate

# ── transport ──
listen: "0.0.0.0:8080"
admin_listen: "127.0.0.1:8081"
admin_require_mtls: true                      # false waives the exposed-admin mTLS guard (scary on purpose)
# tls:
#   cert: { file: /run/secrets/tls-cert.pem }
#   key:  { file: /run/secrets/tls-key.pem }
# admin_tls:
#   cert:      { file: /run/secrets/admin-cert.pem }
#   key:       { file: /run/secrets/admin-key.pem }
#   client_ca: { file: /run/secrets/admin-ca.pem }

# ── IDENTITY PROVIDERS: define once, reference by bare name ──
identity-providers:
  admin-tokens: { module: admin-tokens, token: { env: BUSBAR_ADMIN_TOKEN } }
  # corp-ad:
  #   module: ad                                             # a `kind: auth` plugin
  #   settings: { server: "ldaps://corp", base_dn: "dc=corp" }
  #   max_admin_scope: read-only                             # `read-only` | `full` ONLY; OMIT it
  #                                                          # for read-only (most restrictive)
  #   browser_login: { client_id: busbar-web }               # presence ⇒ a hosted-login button

# ── AUTH: identity (roles) + signed keys ──
auth:
  signing_key: { file: /run/secrets/busbar-signing.key }    # REQUIRED with `keys` below; rotate =
  #                                                          # revoke-all; fleet-shared. Generate one
  #                                                          # with `busbar --generate-signing-key`.
  chain: [keys]                                              # built-in signed-key verifier (bare, no definition)
  # chain: [keys, corp-ad]
  admin_auth: [admin-tokens]
  role_bindings: {}                                          # NESTED BY PROVIDER NAME; pure auth, e.g.:
  # role_bindings:
  #   corp-ad:
  #     growth-eng: { allowed_pools: [fast], group: growth }
  #     platform:   { group: acme, admin_scope: full }       # allowed_pools omitted = ALL pools

# ── GROUPS: the ONE limit tree (also runtime-mutable over the Admin API: GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/
#    DELETE /api/v1/admin/groups — "raise Alice's budget" = PATCH her leaf's limits) ──
groups:
  acme:                                                     # org ceiling
    limits:
      - { requests: 500, per: minute }
      - { budget: 1000000, per: month }
  growth:                                                   # a team under the org
    parent: acme
    limits:
      - { requests: 50, per: minute }
      - { budget: 200000, per: month }
    child_default:                                          # per-HEAD budget stamped onto each
      limits:                                               # user leaf auto-provisioned under this
        - { budget: 2000, per: month }                      # team (nearest-ancestor wins)
  # A USER is just a LEAF GROUP parented to their team: the personal budget is the leaf's own
  # limits, always sub-capped by the team ceiling (the chain ANDs, so per-user budgets can never
  # sum past the team pool). Enforcement walks user -> team -> org and ANDs every limit.
  user:bob:
    parent: growth
    enabled: true                                           # false = freeze this group
    limits:
      - { requests: 10,   per: minute }
      - { requests: 1000, per: day }
      - { concurrent: 5 }                                   # no `per` = in-flight cap

# ── PRICING: the ONE cost source ──
# Every billable class the plane declares must be configured on the card, on any entry (0 = free;
# a token tier an entry omits is 0): the LLM plane also ledgers every count a provider reports
# beside its tokens (search units, Cohere classifications, web fetches, the tokens a stated total
# counts above its itemized buckets, images, transcription milliseconds, Bedrock guardrail policy
# units), each under its own class.
rate_card:
  sonnet-anthropic: { input_utok: 3.0, output_utok: 15.0, cache_read_utok: 0.3, cache_write_utok: 3.75,
                      units: { search_units: 0, classifications: 0, web_fetch_requests: 0,
                              unitemized_tokens: 0, images: 0, audio_ms: 0,
                              guardrail_automated_reasoning_policies: 0,
                              guardrail_automated_reasoning_policy_units: 0,
                              guardrail_content_policy_image_units: 0, guardrail_content_policy_units: 0,
                              guardrail_contextual_grounding_policy_units: 0,
                              guardrail_sensitive_information_policy_free_units: 0,
                              guardrail_sensitive_information_policy_units: 0,
                              guardrail_topic_policy_units: 0, guardrail_word_policy_units: 0 } }
  sonnet-bedrock:   { input_utok: 2.8, output_utok: 14.0 }
per_request_fee: 0

# ── STORE: plugin + opaque settings ──
store:
  module: memory                              # a durable store is a plugin, e.g.:
  # module: postgres
  # settings: { url: "postgres://host/db" }

# ── PROVIDERS / MODELS (two entries = same model, two providers) ──
providers:
  anthropic: { api_key: { env: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY } }
  bedrock:   { api_key: { env: AWS_BEDROCK_CREDS } }
models:
  sonnet-anthropic: { provider: anthropic, upstream_model: claude-3-5-sonnet }
  sonnet-bedrock:   { provider: bedrock,   upstream_model: anthropic.claude-3-5-sonnet-v1 }

# ── POOLS: pure routing/topology ──
# The `pools:` section carries exactly TWO reserved keys, and that set is CLOSED (1.5.3): `hooks:`
# (a LIST ⇒ ADDITIVE with a pool's own, deduped by name) and `upstream_credentials:` (a SCALAR ⇒ a
# pool's own value REPLACES it). A pool may not be named either of them.
pools:
  upstream_credentials: own                                  # all-pools default
  # hooks: [audit]                                           # all-pools attach (requires a hooks: def)
  fast:
    upstream_credentials: passthrough                        # per-pool override (scalar: REPLACES)
    members:
      - { model: sonnet-anthropic, weight: 1, tier: null, tags: [] }   # `target` -> `model`
      - { model: sonnet-bedrock,   weight: 1 }
    hooks: [cheapest]                                        # derives cost from rate_card
    breaker:  { base_cooldown_secs: 15, max_cooldown_secs: 120,
                trip: { mode: error_rate, window_secs: 30, threshold: 0.5, min_requests: 5, consecutive_n: 3 } }
    failover: { timeout_secs: 120, max_hops: 3, exclusions: [] }       # no deadline_secs/cap aliases
    on_exhausted: reject                                     # | { fallback_pool: cold } | least_bad | { queue: { max_ms } }
    affinity: { mode: session }

# ── HOOKS: the top-level NAMED-DEFINITION map; pools reference by bare name ──
# hooks:                                        # requires plugins.enabled: true + the signed tarball
#   pii:
#     module: busbar-hook-webrequest
#     settings: { url: "https://sidecar.internal/pii" }
#     groups: [engineering]                     # SCOPE: omit = all callers
#     phase: [request, response]                # omit = the four core stages (request/candidate/routing/response)
#     kind: gate
#     prompt: no
#     user: no
#     on_error: reject                          # a bare reserved terminal; a fallback HOOK is `{ hook: <name> }`

# ── PLUGINS (loader) ──
plugins:
  enabled: false
  dir: plugins
  trust: { publishers: [], allow_unsigned: false, allow_third_party: false }
  min_versions: {}

# ── SECURITY / EXPORT / LIMITS ──
security:      { blocked_metadata_hosts: [], allow_metadata_hosts: [], allow_all_metadata: false }
# 1.5.3: the `observability:` block is DELETED. ALL telemetry egress is the `export:` NAMED map —
# `<name>: { module, settings }` — and the SAME module may back SEVERAL named instances:
# export:
#   metrics:  { module: prometheus,          settings: { buffer_seconds: 60 } }   # PULL: serves /metrics
#   req-log:  { module: request-log-webhook, settings: { url: "https://logs.example.com/busbar" } }
#   req-siem: { module: request-log-webhook, settings: { url: "https://siem.internal/ingest" } }
#   traces:   { module: otlp,                settings: { url: "http://localhost:4318/v1/traces" } }
limits:        { upstream_request_timeout_secs: 300, request_body_max_bytes: 33554432,
                 max_inbound_concurrent: 8192, hard_down_cooldown_secs: 1800,
                 reasoning_effort_budgets: { minimal: 1024, low: 4096, medium: 8192, high: 16384 } }

# ── ADVANCED: internal tuning ──
advanced:
  rate_sweep_interval: 256
  usage_flush_interval_ms: 100
  # Every busbar-injected response header is opt-in and defaults OFF; see
  # docs/observability.md#response-headers. Uncomment to opt in:
  # response_headers: { server_timing: false, route_policy: false }
name: file:examples/clean-config-1.5.0.yaml

input:
# First-party plugin metadata consumed by busbar-release fleet tooling.
#
# Fields:
#   repo:          GitHub repo under GetBusbar/
#   kind:          store | secret | auth | hook | export | plane | transport  (busbar plugin kind;
#                  selects the C ABI; every kind ships as its own repo)
#   alias:         short config name (busbar-plugin-pack --alias)
#   crate:         the plugin cdylib's Cargo package name: <repo>-plugin beside the <repo> logic
#                  crate, or <repo> itself for a single-crate plugin
#   version_line:  the semver line current releases live on
#   service:       real backend container its tests need (mysql|postgres|valkey|vault|none)
#   release_gate / gate: historical release-check metadata.
#
# Optional fields:
#   checkout_dir:  local sibling/checkout directory name when it differs from `repo`
#                  (no entry needs it today; kept for the next repo rename)
#   checkout_ref: git ref used by registry consumers [dev].
#   provider_key_census: immutable source capture for the historical config-key census;
#                  fixture, commit, path, constant and sha256 bind the recorded descriptor
#                  to this registered plane owner independently of the captured artifact.
#
# Fleet fields (read by `busbar-release plugin sync` (GetBusbar/busbar-release), the ONE generator: it
# renders every plugin repo's CI caller, toolchain, lint config, deny.toml, workspace dependency table,
# LICENSE and README header from this file, its template/ and fleet/deps.toml, and checks the repos
# against the render). Defaults in brackets:
#   manifest_name  the signed manifest's `name` (the plugin's identity at load) [repo]
#   asset_prefix   the published tarball's filename prefix [repo]
#   description    the manifest's one-line description (also the README header's)
#   ci_service     the backend plugin-ci.yml's Linux leg runs against [service]
#   busbar_checkout  the end-to-end tests build and boot a real busbar from a checkout at the pin [false]
#   macos_test     the macOS leg's test command [cargo test --workspace --locked]
#   extra_test     an extra Linux test command [none]
#   lib_only       build the cdylib with --lib [false]
#   needs_prompt / needs_user   a hook's declared intent, signed into the manifest [none]
#   declares       the plugin's `declares` file (repo-relative), signed into the manifest; it states
#                  the contract-ABI range the plugin supports (`contract_abi`), which the loader
#                  refuses a plugin outside of
#   bundle_image / bundle_env   a runnable container bundle the consumer verification boots [none]
#   keep           repo-specific paths the render does not own: a file under .github/, or a top-level
#                  path (`Dockerfile`, `docker/`). Every repo is a TWIN (owner, 2026-09-30): anything
#                  under .github/ or at the top level that is not rendered, not one of the two crate
#                  dirs (`<kind>-<name>/`, `<kind>-<name>-plugin/`), not Cargo.lock and not kept is drift
#   gitignore      lines the rendered .gitignore carries after the fleet's own [none]
#   notice         lines the rendered NOTICE carries after the fleet's own (a third-party credit) [none]
#   former_names   the signed manifest `name`s this plugin's earlier releases carried, which it still
#                  answers to [none]: a 1.5.5 config naming `module: busbar-webrequest` resolves to the
#                  1.6.0 `busbar-hook-webrequest` (ARCHITECT ruling: 1.5.5 configs load unchanged).
#                  Signed into the manifest (busbar-plugin-pack --former-name, plugin-release.yml's
#                  `former_names` input, the rendered release.yml); a LINKED row answers them too
#                  through its `former.<alias>` row of the root migration table.
#   retired        the `module:` spellings this plugin answered to in an earlier release and no longer
#                  does [none]. Each is a `retired.<kind>.<word>` row of the root migration table
#                  (`[package.metadata.busbar.migration]` in dist/default/Cargo.toml), beside the plugin's
#                  `manifest.<alias>` / `asset.<alias>` rows; boot refuses a retired spelling and
#                  `busbar --migrate-config` rewrites it to the alias (BUSBAR-1.6.0.md §2)
#   pending_crate  registered repository whose crates have not moved in yet [false].
#                  busbar-release plugin check skips its crate-shaped checks until seeded.
#   lang           rust | c [rust]. `c`: the plugin is C sources in `<kind>-<name>/`, built from
#                  busbar_plugin.h alone (decision #84); its CI is plugin-ci.yml's C path (build from the
#                  header at the pin, `dropped_conformance` through load_dropped, RED arm kept), its
#                  callers pass `plugin_lang: c`, and it has no Cargo workspace.

# THE FLEET POLICY (`busbar-release plugin check` holds every repo to it; `busbar-release plugin sync` applies it).
#   busbar_ref  ONE pin for every plugin repo: each repo's `.busbar-ref` is exactly this, every
#               manifest's busbar git rev is its sha, and the rendered callers take busbar's reusable
#               workflows at that sha. Moving it is one edit here, then `busbar-release plugin sync`.
#   name_pattern  every plugin repo is `busbar-<kind>-<name>`, and <kind> is the entry's kind.
#   branches    exactly these branches; dev, qa and main carry the repo ruleset `busbar-release plugin sync` applies (PR + plugin-ci green), main and
#               qa are locked by the org ruleset "release branches: main + qa (owner say-so only)"; any
#               other branch is stale.
fleet:
  busbar_ref: "87b5d5fa1042d26aa1fcfece65f036fe8ee254ec 1.6.0"
  name_pattern: "^busbar-(store|secret|auth|hook|export|plane|transport)-[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$"
  branches: [dev, qa, main]

# Repositories matching plugin naming that are deliberately not plugins.
excluded_repos:
  - hindsight-hook # design docs only — no crate, no workflows, private
  - busbar-hook-headroom # removed from busbar and the site (owner ruling 2026-09-30) — the repo is kept, not a busbar plugin

# THE ROOT MIGRATION TABLE'S FROZEN TEXT (BUSBAR-1.6.0.md §2): operator-visible
# 1.5.5 text naming plugins that are not in the build, which `busbar --migrate-config` and the boot
# refusals print. These rows, then every entry's `retired:` rows, are the root migration table,
# `[package.metadata.busbar.migration]` (dist/default/Cargo.toml), which the composition root hands to the
# kernel; crates/busbar/src/root/tests/migration_table.rs renders it from here and is red on drift (printing the
# table to paste). Every row cites the v1.5.5 tag line it is verbatim from; a value never changes.
migration:
  # v1.5.5:crates/busbar/src/config/migrate.rs:267 (the legacy marker's "is Valkey — artifact")
  renamed_display: Valkey
  # The retired backend's own driver URL scheme, which the rewrite leaves untouched.
  # v1.5.5:crates/busbar/src/config/migrate.rs:2075
  retired_url_scheme: redis
  # The host recorder's install-failure log line (1.5.5's recorder carried its exporter's name).
  # v1.5.5:crates/busbar/src/metrics.rs:331
  snapshot_recorder_failed: "prometheus recorder install failed; /metrics will be empty"
  # 1.4.x governance database. v1.5.5:crates/busbar/src/config/migrate.rs:817, :824, :828
  gov14_module: sqlite
  # v1.5.5:crates/busbar/src/config/migrate.rs:30 (DEFAULT_GOVERNANCE_DB_1_4)
  gov14_db_path: busbar-governance.db
  # v1.5.5:crates/busbar/src/config/migrate.rs:836
  gov14_busy_timeout_key: sqlite_busy_timeout_ms
  # v1.5.5:crates/busbar/src/config/migrate.rs:843
  gov14_change: "governance.db_path -> store: { module: sqlite, settings: { db_path } } (1.4.x's only durable backend was SQLite)"
  # v1.5.5:crates/busbar/src/config_validate/mod.rs:1656 (the empty `store.module` refusal)
  module_examples: "sqlite | postgres | valkey"
  # The store a config with no `store:` block ran on, which the empty-`store.module` refusal names and
  # `--migrate-config` writes in. v1.5.5:crates/busbar/src/config/mod.rs:3026 (GOVERNANCE_STORE_MEMORY);
  # v1.5.5:crates/busbar/src/config_validate/mod.rs:1655
  store_1_5_default: memory
  # The browser-login button brands, in 1.5.5's match order: `<match tokens> : <label> : <icon ref>`, the
  # tokens matched (any) against the lower-cased method name and OIDC issuer host; a method none matches
  # is its title-cased name under the generic icon. v1.5.5:crates/busbar/src/auth/token.rs:1073-1112
  # v1.5.5:crates/busbar/src/export/projection.rs:134 (`module_streams`: the streams each built-in exporter carried, `module:stream`)
  export_module_streams: "prometheus:metrics | request-log-webhook:logs | request-log-file:logs | otlp:traces"
  # v1.5.5:crates/busbar/src/config/mod.rs:3359 (`EXPORT_MODULES`: the order the unknown-exporter refusal lists the built-in exporters in)
  export_modules: "prometheus | request-log-webhook | request-log-file | otlp"
  # v1.5.5:crates/busbar/src/config/migrate_export.rs:245 (the instance `observability.otlp_url` folds into)
  export_trace_instance: "traces"
  # v1.5.5:crates/busbar/src/config/migrate_export.rs:249 (the module `observability.otlp_url` folds into)
  export_trace_module: "otlp"
  # v1.5.5:crates/busbar/src/config/migrate_export.rs:31 (`EXPORT_TYPE_KEY_TO_INSTANCE_NAME`: type key, instance name, module)
  export_type_keys: "prometheus:metrics:prometheus | request-log-webhook:req-log:request-log-webhook | request-log-file:req-log-file:request-log-file | generic-webhook:req-log-audit:request-log-webhook"
  # The 1.x hook registry's URL transport key, and the `module:` it migrates to.
  # v1.5.5:crates/busbar/src/config/migrate.rs:1368, :1369, :1383 (and the words of :142, :1380, :1443)
  hook_1x_url_transport: webhook
  # The export type key the top-level `metrics:` block folds under.
  # v1.5.5:crates/busbar/src/config/migrate.rs:1878 (and the words of :168, :1879, :1886; config/mod.rs:1043)
  metrics_type_key: prometheus
  # v1.5.5:crates/busbar/src/config/mod.rs:1002 (RETIRED_CONFIG_KEYS_1_5_3: the deleted `observability:` block's home)
  observability_home: "the `export:` NAMED map — a `module: prometheus` / `module: request-log-webhook` / `module: otlp` instance (all telemetry egress is now the single `export:` surface)"
  # v1.5.5:crates/busbar/src/config/migrate.rs:1856 (the request-log lift-out's change line)
  observability_log_change: "observability.request_log_webhook_url (+ webhook limits) -> export.request-log-webhook.settings (built-in exporter)"
  # The retired request-log `observability.*` keys and the settings key each folds into (`retired:settings`).
  # v1.5.5:crates/busbar/src/config/migrate.rs:1836, :1839, :1842 (config/mod.rs:1030, :1034, :1038)
  observability_log_keys: "request_log_webhook_url:url | max_inflight_webhook_deliveries:max_inflight_deliveries | webhook_delivery_timeout_secs:delivery_timeout_secs"
  # The export type key the request-log keys fold under. v1.5.5:crates/busbar/src/config/migrate.rs:1854
  observability_log_type_key: request-log-webhook
  # The `observability:` trace-URL key. v1.5.5:crates/busbar/src/config/migrate.rs:1806; config/migrate_export.rs:239
  observability_trace_key: otlp_url
  # Its 1.4.x spelling. v1.5.5:crates/busbar/src/config/migrate.rs:1805
  observability_trace_key_1_4: otlp_endpoint
  # THE 1.5.5 MANIFEST NAMES (`name_1_5_5.<repo>`): the signed manifest `name` each plugin repo's
  # release beside busbar v1.5.5 carried, read off that release's published tarball (manifest.json
  # `name`; every asset is digest-pinned in testing/shadow-oracle/plugin-digests.tsv). An entry whose
  # repo has a row here declares that name in its `former_names:` (`cargo xtask plugin-gates
  # former-names`). Built into 1.5.5 and so without a 1.5.5 manifest, and needing no row:
  # admin-tokens, env, file, prometheus, request-log-file, request-log-webhook, otlp.
  # GetBusbar/busbar-hook-webrequest release v1.0.6: busbar-webrequest-1.0.6-<target>.tar.gz manifest.json name
  name_1_5_5.busbar-hook-webrequest: busbar-webrequest
  # GetBusbar/busbar-secret-vault release v1.0.5: busbar-hashicorp-vault-1.0.5-<target>.tar.gz manifest.json name
  name_1_5_5.busbar-secret-vault: busbar-hashicorp-vault
  # GetBusbar/busbar-store-mysql release v1.0.6: busbar-store-mysql-1.0.6-<target>.tar.gz manifest.json name
  name_1_5_5.busbar-store-mysql: busbar-store-mysql-plugin
  # GetBusbar/busbar-store-postgres release v1.0.6: busbar-store-postgres-1.0.6-<target>.tar.gz manifest.json name
  name_1_5_5.busbar-store-postgres: busbar-store-postgres-plugin
  # GetBusbar/busbar-store-sqlite release v1.0.6: busbar-store-sqlite-1.0.6-<target>.tar.gz manifest.json name
  name_1_5_5.busbar-store-sqlite: busbar-store-sqlite-plugin

    release_gate: optional
    gate: suite

    declares: "auth-oauth/declares.json"
    # OWNER QUESTIONS Q99 (2026-10-01): "KEEP THE SPLIT: busbar-auth-header, busbar-auth-sigv4,

    pending_crate: true
  - repo: busbar-secret-c
    kind: secret

    # every one-letter string literal spells, so no instance census could tell the plugin from text.

    alias: secret-c
    crate: busbar-secret-c
    version_line: "1.0"
    service: none
    release_gate: optional
    gate: suite
    description: "First-party signed kind:secret plugin library, written in C from busbar_plugin.h alone: a self-contained secret source (named values in its own settings), packaged as a droppable busbar plugin. Drop the signed tarball into plugins/."
    declares: "secret-c/declares.json"

    # the generated C header alone, created by `busbar-release plugin new secret c --lang c` and
    # tested by itself through plugin-ci.yml's C path at its pin. First release with the core

    released: false

# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
# Copyright (C) 2026 Busbar Inc and contributors
#
# Verified provider catalog for busbar.
#
# Each entry maps a provider NAME to its wire `protocol`, `base_url`, and an optional `error_map`
# (provider-specific JSON error code -> canonical disposition: billing | rate_limit). Operators
# deploy by referencing a provider name in config.yaml and supplying its key via an env var.
#
# busbar's thesis is "protocols, not providers": it implements a small set of wire protocols
# (anthropic, openai, gemini, bedrock, responses, cohere) natively on both sides, and any provider speaking one of
# those protocols is just a catalog entry here - no new code. A client speaking any protocol can
# target any provider; busbar translates through its superset IR when they differ.
#
# Auth is a per-protocol seam, not a single scheme: most providers use `Authorization: Bearer <key>`,
# gemini uses the `x-goog-api-key` header, and bedrock signs each request with AWS SigV4 (see below).
# Azure OpenAI is supported today via the `auth: api-key` override (a fill-in template is below); Google
# Vertex AI via the `auth: jwt-bearer` OAuth adapter (a fill-in template is below the gemini entry).
# HTTP-status errors (429/5xx/401/...) are classified by the circuit breaker without an error_map;
# error_map is only for provider-specific JSON codes.

# -- Anthropic protocol (/v1/messages) -----------------------------------------------------------
anthropic:
  protocol: anthropic
  base_url: https://api.anthropic.com
  error_map: {}
  # Lane capabilities (see docs/providers.md "Lane capabilities"). The newest Claude generations take
  # reasoning ONLY as adaptive thinking (they 400 on `thinking.budget_tokens`) and reject the forced
  # tool the older structured-output path uses, so they are sent adaptive thinking and native
  # `output_config.format`. Claude Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.x cannot switch thinking off (they reject
  # `thinking: {type: disabled}`), so a reasoning-off ask omits `thinking` on them. Every other model
  # keeps the defaults (budget_tokens, forced tool, `{type: disabled}`). First matching rule wins.
  model_capabilities:
    - models: ["claude-opus-5-5*", "claude-fable-5*"]
      anthropic_adaptive_thinking: true
      native_structured_output: true
      thinking_always_on: true
    - models: ["claude-opus-4-7*", "claude-opus-5*", "claude-sonnet-5*", "claude-fable-5*"]
      anthropic_adaptive_thinking: true
      native_structured_output: true

# z.ai exposes two surfaces. `z.ai` is the Anthropic-compatible coding-agent endpoint
# (/api/anthropic + /v1/messages). `zai-api` (below, in the OpenAI section) is the general
# pay-as-you-go API (OpenAI-compatible, version in the base path). Pick the one your key targets.
z.ai:
  protocol: anthropic
  base_url: https://api.z.ai/api/anthropic
  error_map:
    "1113": billing
    "1302": rate_limit

# -- OpenAI Chat Completions protocol (/v1/chat/completions) --------------------------------------
# Any provider exposing an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions endpoint. The `base_url` is composed
# with `/v1/chat/completions`; the entries below place each provider's prefix accordingly.
openai:
  protocol: openai
  base_url: https://api.openai.com
  error_map:
    insufficient_quota: billing
    rate_limit_exceeded: rate_limit
  # OpenAI's API deprecates `max_tokens`, and its o-series / gpt-5 models reject it: a request that
  # crosses from another protocol writes its output cap as `max_completion_tokens` on this provider.
  # (OpenAI-compatible hosts below keep the default `max_tokens`, which is what they all accept.)
  max_output_key: max_completion_tokens
  # GPT-5.1 and GPT-5.2 accept `reasoning_effort: "none"` (reasoning switched off), so a reasoning-off
  # ask from another protocol is written as "none" on them; every other model omits it (the default).
  model_capabilities:
    - models: ["gpt-5.1", "gpt-5.1-20*", "gpt-5.2", "gpt-5.2-20*"]
      reasoning_none: true

# Oracle OCI Generative AI, the OpenAI-compatible surface (/openai/v1/chat/completions), serving
# OCI's hosted catalog (OpenAI, Meta Llama, xAI, Google, and Cohere models). Since Jan 2026 OCI
# issues plain API keys (Bearer), so NO OCI request-signing is needed - set api_key_env to an env var
# holding the key. REGIONAL: the region is in the host - set it to yours (`us-chicago-1` /
# `us-ashburn-1` carry the broadest model set). Throttling is HTTP 429 (classified by the breaker);
# OCI can also return a 400 carrying `TooManyRequests`/`QuotaExceeded`/`LimitExceeded`, and the
# OpenAI-compat layer may emit OpenAI-style codes - both are mapped. (An OCI Responses transport also
# exists at /openai/v1/responses; add a `protocol: responses` entry if you want it.)
oci-genai:
  protocol: openai
  base_url: https://inference.generativeai.us-chicago-1.oci.oraclecloud.com/openai
  error_map:
    TooManyRequests: rate_limit
    QuotaExceeded: billing
    LimitExceeded: billing
    rate_limit_exceeded: rate_limit
    insufficient_quota: billing

groq:
  protocol: openai
  base_url: https://api.groq.com/openai
  error_map:
    rate_limit_exceeded: rate_limit

# z.ai general API (pay-as-you-go), OpenAI-compatible. The version lives in the base path

# Google Vertex AI (Gemini) speaks the SAME gemini protocol, but at a project/location-scoped URL and
# with OAuth (`auth: jwt-bearer` — a signed service-account JWT exchanged for an auto-refreshed bearer)
# instead of an API key. project + location are per-account, so it is not shipped as a live entry -
# copy this template into your config.yaml providers map and fill in your values. `api_key` resolves
# to the service-account JSON. For a key file use `api_key: { file: /absolute/key.json }`.
# Vertex returns Google's `google.rpc`
# error codes (same `status` tokens as native gemini), so the error_map mirrors gemini's.
#
#   gemini-vertex:
#     protocol: gemini
#     base_url: https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com
#     path_base: /v1/projects/YOUR_PROJECT/locations/us-central1/publishers/google/models
#     auth: jwt-bearer
#     api_key: { env: VERTEX_SA_KEY }                  # resolves to service-account JSON
#     error_map:
#       RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: rate_limit
#
# Claude-on-Vertex is the SAME shape on the `anthropic` protocol: busbar moves the model into the URL
# (`:rawPredict`) and adds the required `anthropic_version` body field automatically. Just point
# path_base at the `anthropic` publisher:
#
#   claude-vertex:
#     protocol: anthropic
#     base_url: https://us-central1-aiplatform.googleapis.com
#     path_base: /v1/projects/YOUR_PROJECT/locations/us-central1/publishers/anthropic/models
#     auth: jwt-bearer
#     api_key: { env: VERTEX_SA_KEY }
#     error_map: {}

# -- AWS Bedrock protocol (Converse / ConverseStream) ---------------------------------------------
# Auth is native AWS SigV4: set this provider's api_key_env to the AWS credentials as
# `ACCESS_KEY_ID:SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` or `ACCESS_KEY_ID:SECRET_ACCESS_KEY:SESSION_TOKEN`. The region is
# parsed from the base_url host (`bedrock-runtime.<region>.amazonaws.com`) - set it to your region.
# Streaming requests use ConverseStream; busbar decodes the binary
# application/vnd.amazon.eventstream frames and translates them to the caller's protocol.
bedrock:
  protocol: bedrock
  base_url: https://bedrock-runtime.us-east-1.amazonaws.com
  error_map:
    ThrottlingException: rate_limit
    ServiceQuotaExceededException: billing
  # Lane capabilities for Claude on Bedrock (model ids carry an `anthropic.` provider segment, behind
  # an optional inference-profile prefix such as `us.`). The newest generations take reasoning ONLY
  # as adaptive thinking and structured output natively (Converse `outputConfig`), exactly as on the
  # first-party `anthropic` entry. Claude Sonnet 4.5, Haiku 4.5, Opus 4.5 and Opus 4.6 support
  # Converse structured outputs per AWS's supported-model list
  # (https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/claude-messages-structured-outputs.html);
  # they keep budget thinking. Claude Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.x cannot switch thinking off, so a
  # reasoning-off ask omits `thinking` on them instead of writing `{type: disabled}`. Written in flow
  # (JSON) style. First matching rule wins.
  model_capabilities: [
    {"models": ["*anthropic.claude-opus-5-5*", "*anthropic.claude-fable-5*"],
     "anthropic_adaptive_thinking": true, "native_structured_output": true,
     "thinking_always_on": true},
    {"models": ["*anthropic.claude-opus-4-7*", "*anthropic.claude-opus-5*",
                "*anthropic.claude-sonnet-5*", "*anthropic.claude-fable-5*"],
     "anthropic_adaptive_thinking": true, "native_structured_output": true},
    {"models": ["*anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5*", "*anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5*",
                "*anthropic.claude-opus-4-5*", "*anthropic.claude-opus-4-6*"],
     "native_structured_output": true}
  ]

# -- Cohere v2 Chat protocol (/v2/chat) -----------------------------------------------------------
# Cohere's Command family via the v2 Chat API. Bearer auth; the protocol targets /v2/chat. Errors
# are signalled by HTTP status (classified by the breaker), so error_map is empty.
cohere:
  protocol: cohere
  base_url: https://api.cohere.com
  error_map: {}

# SPDX-License-Identifier: AGPL-3.0-or-later
# Copyright (C) 2026 Matthew Jackson
#
# busbar deployment configuration (config.yaml).
#
# Two-file model:
#   • providers.yaml  — the vetted provider catalog (protocol, base_url, error_map). Shipped.
#   • config.yaml     — THIS file: your deployment. References providers by NAME and supplies their
#                       keys via environment-variable names (never the keys themselves).
#
# Flow: clients call busbar; busbar routes each request to a `model` or a `pool` of models, tracks
# per-member health with a circuit breaker, and translates between protocols when a client speaks a
# different wire format than the chosen backend. Secrets are never written here — configure the
# environment-variable NAME that holds each key; dollar-brace placeholders are expanded at load time
# (see `client_tokens` below). Every such placeholder's variable must be set in the environment.
#
# This example builds up from the simplest case to progressively richer pools — read top to bottom.

# ── Listen address ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
listen: "0.0.0.0:8080"

# ── Client authentication ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# mode:
#   token        — clients must send `Authorization: Bearer <token>` matching an allowlist below.
#   passthrough  — the client's own key is forwarded to the upstream provider (busbar adds nothing).
#   none         — open relay (no client auth; dev only).
# When governance is enabled (bottom of file), virtual keys supersede this for proxied requests.
auth:
  mode: token
  client_tokens:
    - "${BUSBAR_CLIENT_TOKEN}"        # one or more allowed client tokens (env-expanded)

# ── Providers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Reference a provider NAME from providers.yaml and give the env var holding its key. protocol /
# base_url / error_map are inherited from providers.yaml; override here only in unusual cases.
providers:
  anthropic:
    api_key_env: ANTHROPIC_KEY
  openai:
    api_key_env: OPENAI_KEY
  gemini:
    api_key_env: GEMINI_KEY
  z.ai:
    api_key_env: ZAI_KEY
  bedrock:
    # Bedrock auth is AWS SigV4: the key env holds `ACCESS_KEY_ID:SECRET_ACCESS_KEY[:SESSION_TOKEN]`.
    api_key_env: AWS_BEDROCK_CREDS

# ── Models ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Each model names its provider, a per-model concurrency cap (max_concurrent), and an optional
# lifetime request budget (max_requests; -1 = unlimited). A model is a "lane" with its own semaphore
# and health state. Clients can target a model directly (`POST /<model>/v1/messages`) or via a pool.
models:
  claude-sonnet:
    provider: anthropic
    max_concurrent: 20
    max_requests: -1
  claude-haiku:
    provider: anthropic
    max_concurrent: 40
    max_requests: -1
  gpt-4o:
    provider: openai
    max_concurrent: 20
    max_requests: -1
  gpt-4o-mini:
    provider: openai
    max_concurrent: 50
    max_requests: -1
  gemini-1.5-pro:
    provider: gemini
    max_concurrent: 15
    max_requests: -1
  glm-4.6:
    provider: z.ai
    max_concurrent: 10
    max_requests: -1
  claude-sonnet-bedrock:
    provider: bedrock
    max_concurrent: 20
    max_requests: -1

# ── Pools ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# A pool is a named set of weighted member models. Its members' concurrency caps stack into one
# aggregate, and the breaker fails a request over to a healthy member when one is tripped. Target a
# pool with `POST /<pool>/v1/messages` (or the `model` field for `/v1/chat/completions`).
pools:

  # 1) Simplest pool: a single model. Useful to give a model a stable public name / alias.
  haiku:
    members:
      - target: claude-haiku

  # 2) Basic round-robin: equal-weight members. Smooth weighted round-robin spreads load evenly;
  #    if one member trips, traffic shifts to the others automatically.
  fast:
    members:
      - target: claude-haiku
      - target: gpt-4o-mini

  # 3) Weighted split: send ~80% to the first member, ~20% to the second (e.g. canarying a model).
  balanced:
    members:
      - target: claude-sonnet
        weight: 8
      - target: gpt-4o
        weight: 2

  # 4) Context-length aware: declare each member's max context window. A request that is too large
  #    for one member fails over to a larger-context member instead of erroring — without penalizing
  #    the smaller lane (it was healthy; the request simply didn't fit).
  long-context:
    members:
      - target: claude-sonnet
        context_max: 200000
      - target: gemini-1.5-pro
        context_max: 2000000

  # 5) Failover tuning: bound how long/often busbar retries across members for one request.
  #    deadline_secs — give up after this wall-clock budget. cap — at most this many failover hops.
  #    exclusions — member models to never fail a request over TO (e.g. an expensive last resort).
  resilient:
    members:
      - target: claude-sonnet
        weight: 3
      - target: gpt-4o
        weight: 2
      - target: glm-4.6
        weight: 1
    failover:
      deadline_secs: 30
      cap: 3
      exclusions:
        - glm-4.6        # kept in the pool for capacity, but never used as a failover destination

  # 6) Exhaustion policy + fallback pool: when every member is tripped/at-capacity, choose what to do.
  #    action: reject | status_503 | least_bad | fallback_pool:<name>
  #      least_bad      — serve the member whose cooldown expires soonest rather than 503.
  #      fallback_pool  — route to another pool entirely (loop-guarded).
  primary:
    members:
      - target: claude-sonnet
      - target: gpt-4o
    on_exhausted:
      action: fallback_pool:overflow      # when primary is fully exhausted, spill to `overflow`

  # The fallback target referenced above. Its own exhaustion policy serves the soonest-healthy member.
  overflow:
    members:
      - target: claude-haiku
      - target: gpt-4o-mini
      - target: glm-4.6
    on_exhausted:
      action: least_bad

  # 7) Session affinity + cross-protocol: pin a conversation to one member while it's healthy (so
  #    cache/state stays warm), keyed by a request header. Members here span THREE protocols
  #    (Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini) — a client speaking any one of them reaches all three, because
  #    busbar translates losslessly through its superset IR.
  smart:
    members:
      - target: claude-sonnet
        weight: 2
      - target: gpt-4o
        weight: 2
      - target: gemini-1.5-pro
        weight: 1
    affinity:
      mode: session              # stick to one member per session while it stays healthy
      header_name: x-session-id  # the request header carrying the session key (this is the default)

# ── Observability (optional) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Prometheus `/metrics` is always on and needs no config. These two sinks are opt-in:
#   otlp_endpoint            — export OpenTelemetry traces (OTLP/HTTP) to a collector.
#   request_log_webhook_url  — fire-and-forget a JSON request-log POST per request.
# observability:
#   otlp_endpoint: "http://localhost:4318/v1/traces"
#   request_log_webhook_url: "https://logs.example.com/busbar"

# ── Governance (optional) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# When enabled, clients authenticate with busbar-issued VIRTUAL KEYS (managed via the admin API)
# instead of the static `auth` tokens above. Each key carries allowed-pools (403), a spend budget
# (402 when exceeded), and RPM/TPM rate limits (429). Enforcement state persists in embedded SQLite.
# governance:
#   enabled: true
#   db_path: /var/lib/busbar/governance.db
#   admin_token: "${BUSBAR_ADMIN_TOKEN}"      # guards the /admin/keys management API
#   price_per_request_cents: 1                # flat per-request budget charge
#   price_per_1k_tokens_cents: 50             # plus per-1000-token charge (from response usage)
name: file:tests/migration-corpus/from-tags/v0.14.0_config.yaml

# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
# Copyright (C) 2026 Busbar Inc and contributors
#
# Busbar config for the REAL-provider (Anthropic) latency benchmark. One provider, one model named
# for a real Anthropic model id (Busbar sends the model-entry key upstream), one single-member pool.
# Token auth with a fixed bench token; governance OFF (we measure the proxy hot path, not the control
# plane). The upstream Anthropic key comes from the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY env var — never written here.
#
# Methodology: the bench drives BOTH
#   direct : loadgen -> api.anthropic.com           (Anthropic Messages API, x-api-key)
#   busbar : loadgen -> busbar -> api.anthropic.com  (Anthropic ingress, same upstream model)
# and subtracts per percentile. Anthropic's latency is in BOTH paths and cancels in the delta, so
# `busbar - direct` is Busbar's added overhead — against real provider jitter.
listen: "127.0.0.1:8080"

auth:
  mode: token
  client_tokens:
    - "bench-token"

providers:
  anthropic:
    api_key_env: ANTHROPIC_API_KEY

models:
  # The entry KEY is the upstream model id Busbar forwards to Anthropic (there is no separate
  # upstream-model field). Keep this identical to the model the direct path calls, so both paths hit
  # the same Anthropic model and the delta is pure Busbar overhead.
  claude-haiku-4-5-20251001:
    provider: anthropic
    max_concurrent: 64
    default_max_tokens: 16

pools:
  bench-pool:
    members:
      - target: claude-haiku-4-5-20251001

# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0

#

# Two-file model:
#   • providers.yaml  — the vetted provider catalog (protocol, base_url, error_map). Shipped.
#   • config.yaml     — THIS file: your deployment. References providers by NAME and supplies their
#                       keys as SECRET REFERENCES (never the keys themselves).
#
# Flow: clients call busbar; busbar routes each request to a `model` or a `pool` of models, tracks
# per-member health with a circuit breaker, and translates between protocols when a client speaks a
# different wire format than the chosen backend. Secrets are never written here - every secret value
# is a SECRET REFERENCE resolved through a secret module: `{ env: VAR }` (environment variable),
# `{ file: /path }` (file contents), or `{ module: <secret-plugin>, settings: {…} }`.
#
# This example builds up from the simplest case to progressively richer pools — read top to bottom.

# ── Listen address ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# ── Admin plane (always its own listener) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The admin API (/api/v1/admin/…) ALWAYS runs on its OWN listener — it is never served on the data
# `listen` above. The management plane is privileged, so it stays isolated with its own TLS/mTLS,
# bind, and firewall posture, independent of public LLM traffic. `admin_listen` defaults to loopback
# (127.0.0.1:8081), so a zero-config deployment boots with admin reachable only on-host.
#
# SECURITY: a network-exposed admin_listen (any non-loopback bind) REFUSES TO BOOT unless it requires
# client-certificate mTLS via admin_tls.client_ca. A loopback bind (127.0.0.1 / ::1 / localhost)
# is exempt. To run a token-only admin plane on an exposed address on purpose — e.g. behind a mesh
# that terminates mTLS — set `admin_insecure: true` to waive the guard deliberately.
#
# admin_listen: "127.0.0.1:8081"    # default; set an exposed address (+ admin_tls) to manage off-host
# admin_tls:
#   cert:      { file: /etc/busbar/admin-cert.pem }
#   key:       { file: /etc/busbar/admin-key.pem }
#   client_ca: { file: /etc/busbar/admin-client-ca.pem }   # present ⇒ mTLS required on the admin plane
# admin_insecure: false                                  # true ⇒ waive the exposed-admin mTLS guard

# ── Client authentication ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# auth.chain - an ORDERED list of auth module entries identifying the caller. `keys` is the
# built-in signed-key verifier: clients present busbar-minted keys (POST /api/v1/admin/keys).
# An IdP module (a `kind: auth` plugin) is a map entry carrying its typed fields + settings, e.g.
#   - ad: { max_admin_scope: full, settings: { server: "ldaps://corp" } }
# An EMPTY chain is an open relay (no client auth; dev only). upstream_credentials controls whose
# key hits the provider: `own` (default - busbar's configured key) or `passthrough` (forward the
# caller's key). admin_auth gates /api/v1/admin/* (default [admin-tokens]); role_bindings map an
# IdP module's asserted ROLES to policy (allowed_pools / group / admin_scope), NESTED BY MODULE.

    - keys
  upstream_credentials: own
  admin_auth:
    - admin-tokens: { token: { env: BUSBAR_ADMIN_TOKEN } }   # guards the admin API (mint keys etc.)
  # role_bindings:
  #   ad:
  #     growth-eng: { allowed_pools: [fast], group: growth }
  #     platform:   { group: acme, admin_scope: full }       # allowed_pools omitted = ALL pools

  #                                                          # = generated on first boot (0600)

# ── Providers ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Reference a provider NAME from providers.yaml and give a secret reference for its key. protocol /
# base_url / error_map are inherited from providers.yaml; override here only in unusual cases.

    # inferred from real traffic via the breaker + half-open probe).
    #   mode: none   — passive only (default).
    #        dead   — periodically re-probe ONLY tripped lanes so they recover faster.
    #        active — periodically probe EVERY lane (sends a tiny billable request per interval).

    #   mode: dead
    #   interval_secs: 30   # default 30
    #   timeout_secs: 5     # default 5

    api_key: { env: OPENAI_KEY }
  gemini:
    api_key: { env: GEMINI_KEY }
  z.ai:
    api_key: { env: ZAI_KEY }

    # Bedrock auth is AWS SigV4: the secret holds `ACCESS_KEY_ID:SECRET_ACCESS_KEY[:SESSION_TOKEN]`.
    api_key: { env: AWS_BEDROCK_CREDS }

# ── Models ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Each model names its provider, a per-model concurrency cap (max_concurrent), and an optional
# lifetime request budget (max_requests; -1 = unlimited). A model is a "lane" with its own semaphore
# and health state. Clients can target a model directly (`POST /<model>/v1/messages`) or via a pool.
#
# default_max_tokens (optional): output-token default injected ONLY when a cross-protocol translation
# targets a backend that REQUIRES max_tokens (the Anthropic Messages API) and the source request
# omitted it — legal for OpenAI clients, which rely on the server default. Without it, such a request
# 400s with `max_tokens: Field required`. Unset falls back to a conservative 4096; a caller-supplied
# max_tokens is always preserved. No effect on same-protocol passthrough. Must be > 0 when set.
# (Bedrock Converse defaults maxTokens when omitted, so it needs no injection.)

  claude-sonnet:

    max_concurrent: 20
    max_requests: -1

    #                   # reasoning ask (OpenAI reasoning_effort / Gemini thinkingBudget) reaches

    #                   # dropped (warned) and never sent, so a non-thinking model never 400s.

    provider: anthropic
    max_concurrent: 40
    max_requests: -1
  gpt-4o:
    provider: openai
    max_concurrent: 20
    max_requests: -1
  gpt-4o-mini:
    provider: openai
    max_concurrent: 50
    max_requests: -1
  gemini-1.5-pro:
    provider: gemini
    max_concurrent: 15
    max_requests: -1
  glm-4.6:
    provider: z.ai
    max_concurrent: 10
    max_requests: -1
  claude-sonnet-bedrock:
    provider: bedrock
    max_concurrent: 20
    max_requests: -1

# ── Pools ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# A pool is a named set of weighted member models. Its members' concurrency caps stack into one
# aggregate, and the breaker fails a request over to a healthy member when one is tripped. Target a
# pool with `POST /<pool>/v1/messages` (or the `model` field for `/v1/chat/completions`).
